chunks.content: 96 Don’t Let Red Lines Derail Your Deal Hi Sara, Let’s talk about a universal truth in deal-making: everyone’s happy with the first draft of a purchase agreement...until those dreaded red lines show up. The initial draft goes out, and spirits are high. It’s a moment of optimism, closing seems within reach and simple. But the second round of edits between the parties’ attorneys? If you’re not careful, that’s when the wheels come off, and chaos ensues. Resentment brews. Tempers flare. Attorneys fees mount and people blame the other side. Why does this happen? Sticker Shock on Legal Fees: Those mounting invoices don’t exactly inspire goodwill. Rejection Stings: When your carefully crafted offer gets marked up or outright rejected, it can feel very personal. The Lawyer Factor: Let’s face it, some attorneys are more sandpaper than silk—grating and uncooperative. Add in the “telephone game” between two parties, and it’s a recipe for escalation. By this point, the excitement of the deal is a distant memory, replaced by glares across the negotiation table. But it doesn’t have to be this way. How to Keep Your Deal on Track: Start Fair: A balanced initial agreement minimizes the back-and-forth drama. Nail the LOI: A solid Letter of intent sets the stage for smoother negotiations in the definitive agreements. Choose the Right Attorney: A collaborative, experienced deal attorney can save your deal—and your sanity. If you choose a combative attorney or a lawyer who doesn’t primarily work in deals, you may be throwing a wildcard into the mix that the deal can’t recover from. The bottom line? A little upfront effort and the right professionals can keep your deal moving forward, even through those inevitable red-line edits.
